item.title: OpenAI Says It Has Cracked One of Math’s ‘Millennium Problems’
OpenAI says it cracked 90-year-old maths problem in 88 hours
item.description:
# OpenAI says it cracked 90-year-old maths problem in 88 hours OpenAI says it has found a solution to a decades-old advanced maths problem in a matter of hours using a new artificial intelligence (AI) model and thousands of AI bots.
The ChatGPT-maker [said on Tuesday](https://openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/) that by focusing a group of roughly 10,000 AI agents, or AI bots that undertake tasks somewhat autonomously, it solved a notoriously difficult maths problem in just 88 hours.

item.title: Artificial intelligence and the future of maternal and child health
item.description:
## Contributors from the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) discuss the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI) in maternal and child health, highlighting its applications in research, clinical decision-making, and public health ### AI embedded in clinical care AI-mediated approaches are increasingly being integrated directly into interventions and clinical care. They are expected to shorten the diagnostic odyssey, accelerate access to specialized care, and facilitate the development of personalized medicine approaches. Such applications are wide-ranging – for example, using AI in conjunction with other assistive technologies to improve intuitive control of prosthetic limbs, creating an AI-driven total parenteral nutritional composition platform for dietary care of premature infants, AI-assisted assessment of gamete and embryo quality for in vitro fertilization, chatbots that aid in the diagnosis of and patient education for congenital anomalies or rare diseases, and predictive modeling to help identify patients at risk for developing gynecological, infectious, maternal, and pediatric conditions. Across these applications, research priorities include prospective validation, assessment of real-world performance and safety, and understanding how AI outputs influence clinical decision-making and patient outcomes.

item.title: NSA looks to AI to help analysts sift through vast data troves
item.description:
## The tools can speed up work that takes days or weeks, the agency’s cybersecurity chief said. The National Security Agency is leaning into artificial intelligence tools to process mass volumes of data it collects, allowing analysts to sort through tasks and find anomalies faster, a top official said Tuesday.
Late last month, NSA deputy director Tim Kosiba said that the agency wants access to a wide range of models and is [engaging](https://www.nextgov.com/artificial-intelligence/2026/08/nsa-wants-access-all-ai-models-top-official-says/415672/) heavily with frontier AI companies.
